land.text: Gibraltar, captured on 4 August 1704 by Anglo-Dutch forces; ceded to Great Britain in perpetuity at Utrecht in 1713

predecessors.note: The Kingdom of Spain and Kingdom of Great Britain dossiers book the transfer at the 13 July 1713 treaty; this dossier starts at the 1704 capture and draws 1704-1713 as contested.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Gibraltar row (its British Colonial Empire aggregate, 1706-1999, is a separate dossier). The infobox area is 6.8 km2, far below the grid cell, so the keyframe is one small patch. The pages give no boundary; the isthmus and the 1713 wording of the cession are not on the pages opened.

ledger.note: 4 August 1704: Anglo-Dutch forces under Rooke take Gibraltar. 'On 4 August, seeing all was lost, Don Diego agreed to terms'; 'In 1704, Anglo-Dutch forces captured Gibraltar from Spain during the War of the Spanish Succession' (Gibraltar page). It was held in Charles III's name, but by English troops at English cost.

August 1704: Gibraltar becomes ground contested between Philip V's Spain and the Allies: after the Battle of Málaga (24 August) 'French and Spanish troops battered at the land approaches'. The page dates neither the start nor the end of the 1704-05 siege.
August 1704: held by English troops at English cost, drawn as the colony tint of England. 'Gibraltar was held in Charles III's name, but it was held by English troops at English cost.'
1 May 1707: England ends in the Acts of Union. 'The Acts came into effect on 1 May 1707'; the colony tint passes to Great Britain.
1 May 1707: Gibraltar is a possession of the new Kingdom of Great Britain.

13 July 1713: Spain cedes Gibraltar. 'In Article X, Spain ceded the strategic ports of Gibraltar and Menorca' ('Spain under Philip V signed separate peace treaties with Savoy and Great Britain at Utrecht on 13 July'); the Gibraltar page: 'ceded to Great Britain in perpetuity under the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713'. Menorca, ceded in the same article, is not part of this dossier.

16 June 1779: Spain besieges Gibraltar. 'On 16 June 1779, the Spanish issued what was in effect a declaration of war against Great Britain' and the blockade followed; the garrison was besieged 'from June 1779 to February 1783'. The 1727 siege was unsuccessful and is not dated beyond the year.
7 February 1783: 'The siege was finally lifted on 7 February 1783' after the failed Grand Assault of 13 September 1782; the Treaty of Versailles of September 1783 'left Gibraltar with the British'.
1 January 1801: 'Great Britain was merged into the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'; the tint passes to the United Kingdom.
1 January 1801: Gibraltar is a possession of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

25 June 1830: 'Gibraltar was declared a crown colony on 25 June 1830.' Same state, same colour; today a British Overseas Territory. The 1967 referendum (10 September), the 1969 closure of the Spanish border and its reopening (partly 1982, fully 1985) moved no border.

wars.name: Capture of Gibraltar
wars.outcome: Anglo-Dutch capture on 4 August 1704 (War of the Spanish Succession); held against a Franco-Spanish siege; ceded to Britain at Utrecht in 1713.
wars.note: The page gives no end date for the 1704-05 siege, so 1705 is not stated on it.

wars.name: Siege of Gibraltar (1727)
wars.outcome: An unsuccessful Spanish siege; no change of sovereignty.
wars.note: Only the year and the result are on the Gibraltar page.

wars.name: Great Siege of Gibraltar
wars.outcome: British victory: the Grand Assault of 13 September 1782 failed, the siege was lifted on 7 February 1783 and the Treaty of Versailles left Gibraltar with Britain; Spain kept Menorca.
wars.note: Relief convoys on 25 January 1780, 12 April 1781 and 16-18 October 1782.

certainty.note: A coastal peninsula of 6.8 km2; the sea is the border on three sides. The pages opened give no line for the isthmus, which is the only disputed edge.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (the scope names Gibraltar as lacking in Cliopatria); five pages. Double-booking to reconcile: the kingdom-of-spain and kingdom-of-great-britain dossiers (eu-12-m, eu-11) already book Gibraltar and Menorca as a Spain loss and a British gain on 13 July 1713, with no 1704-1713 entry; this dossier starts at the 1704 capture, draws 1704-1713 as contested with Spain and as a colony tint of England then Great Britain, and so duplicates 1713-onwards cells (6.8 km2) that the Great Britain dossier draws as direct land. The reviewer should choose: keep this dossier (type colony, tint of the sovereign) and delete the Gibraltar part of the British gain, or drop this dossier. The metropole chain is England to 1 May 1707, Great Britain to 1 January 1801, the United Kingdom after. The end year is 2024, the project's close for living states (as in united-kingdom and kingdom-of-spain); the state is alive, so the 1801 vassal_start has no end and there is no dissolve event [Reviewer eu-12-x, 2026-10-25: end moved from 2026 and the two confidence-1 2026 events (vassal_end, dissolve) removed, since Gibraltar did not dissolve]. Menorca (ceded in the same Article X; the Great Britain page: 'Britain lost the island of Minorca in 1756'; the Spain and Great Britain dossiers book 1783, 1798 and 1802) is not Gibraltar; a separate British Menorca dossier is the next candidate (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Not opened: the Treaty text (the page quotes no wording on the town, castle and port, nor on a reversion clause), the 1704-05 siege's end, the 1967 and 1969 events beyond the Gibraltar page's one line. No gazetteer gaps: the Natural Earth country Gibraltar is used.
